Bauschke–Tung Theorem 7.1 then realizes the Gaussian vector sequence as an orbit of a firmly nonexpansive map with unique fixed point. value.rationale: The 2026 source introduced a new nonlinear ergodic counterexample and a qualitative strong-convergence theorem for many meshes, without its exact speed. A continuum of exact rates and constants for 1/2<alpha<1 quantifies how averaging may converge arbitrarily slowly in the same orbit class even while the unaveraged iterates fail to converge strongly. The invariant is the natural squared norm of actual Cesàro means, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
